deathCause.detail: Contemporary and later accounts commonly attribute Wenceslaus's final illness to tuberculosis, but the diagnosis cannot be medically certain.
deathCause.detailCn: 同时代与后世记载通常将其最后的疾病归为肺结核，但无法作出具有现代医学意义的确诊。

events.label: Succeeded to the Bohemian crown under a Brandenburg regency
events.labelCn: 在勃兰登堡摄政下继承波希米亚王位
events.note: His father Ottokar II was killed at Marchfeld; seven-year-old Wenceslaus inherited the crown, while Otto V of Brandenburg governed until 1283.

events.label: Returned to Prague after the Brandenburg guardianship
events.labelCn: 勃兰登堡监护期结束后返回布拉格
events.note: His return ended the most restrictive phase of Otto V's guardianship, though noble factions continued to dominate government for several years.

events.label: Executed Záviš of Falkenstein and began personal rule
events.labelCn: 处决法尔肯施泰因的扎维什，开始亲政
events.note: The fall of the dominant magnate Záviš ended the regency-era struggle for control of the young king.

events.label: Acquired the Duchy of Cracow and Lesser Poland
events.labelCn: 取得克拉科夫公国与小波兰
events.note: Invited by Polish lords after Henry IV Probus's death, Wenceslaus gained a decisive base for his later Polish kingship.

events.label: Crowned King of Bohemia at Prague
events.labelCn: 在布拉格加冕为波希米亚国王

events.label: Crowned King of Poland at Gniezno
events.labelCn: 在格涅兹诺加冕为波兰国王
events.note: The Polish coronation converted his regional foothold at Cracow into a royal claim over Poland.

events.label: Reformed the coinage and issued the mining code
events.labelCn: 改革币制并颁行矿业法典
events.note: The Prague groschen and the Ius regale montanorum turned the Kutná Hora silver boom into a durable fiscal foundation for the crown.

events.label: Secured the Hungarian crown for his son Wenceslaus
events.labelCn: 为儿子瓦茨拉夫取得匈牙利王冠
events.note: After Andrew III's death, Wenceslaus accepted the Hungarian crown for his son, who was crowned as Ladislaus V.

events.label: Died at Prague
events.note: He died aged 33, probably from pulmonary tuberculosis, and was succeeded in Bohemia and Poland by Wenceslaus III.

sourceNote: Biografický slovník českých zemí (Czech Academy of Sciences); Czech National Archives authority record; Treccani; Croatian Encyclopedia; Deutsche Biographie.
notes:
Wenceslaus II turned a precarious child succession into the high point of late Přemyslid power. From Bohemia he extended authority into Kraków and Poland, while his fiscal reforms based on Kutná Hora silver strengthened royal government. In 1301 he also obtained the Hungarian crown for his son, briefly projecting his dynasty across three kingdoms. His early death left this expansion dependent on Wenceslaus III, whose assassination ended the male Přemyslid line the following year.

Confidence / caveats: He was born on 27 September 1271 and died in Prague on 21 June 1305. Pulmonary tuberculosis is the usual attribution for his death but is not certain by modern diagnostic standards. His mother Kunigunda of Halych and wives Judith of Habsburg and Elisabeth Richeza are not yet in the roster.

events.label: Killed at the Battle of Crécy
Received the County of Luxembourg
events.note: Henry VII transferred Luxembourg to his son John before the Bohemian expedition, giving the young prince an independent hereditary base.

events.label: Married Elisabeth of Bohemia and claimed the Bohemian crown
events.labelCn: 与波希米亚的伊丽莎白结婚并取得波希米亚王位继承依据
events.note: The marriage to the Přemyslid princess Elisabeth gave John a dynastic basis for challenging Henry of Carinthia and entering Bohemia as king.

events.label: Was crowned King of Bohemia at Prague
events.labelCn: 在布拉格加冕为波希米亚国王
events.note: John and Elisabeth were crowned at Prague, formally establishing Luxembourg rule over the Bohemian kingdom.

events.label: Participated in the contested German royal election
events.labelCn: 参与争议性的德意志王位选举
events.note: John was considered in the succession struggle after Henry VII's death but ultimately supported Louis of Bavaria against Frederick the Fair.

events.label: Fought for Louis of Bavaria at Mühldorf
events.labelCn: 在米尔多夫战役中支持巴伐利亚的路易作战
events.note: John supported Louis of Bavaria in the Battle of Mühldorf against the Habsburg claimant Frederick the Fair and received political and territorial rewards for his support.

events.label: Participated in a crusading campaign against Lithuania
events.labelCn: 参加针对立陶宛的十字军远征
events.note: John joined the Teutonic Order's winter campaign against pagan Lithuania, one of several crusading expeditions in which he participated.

events.label: Renounced his claim to the Polish crown at Trenčín
events.labelCn: 在特伦钦放弃波兰王位宣称
events.note: The settlement with Casimir III ended John's claim to the Polish crown while strengthening Bohemian overlordship over the Silesian principalities.

events.label: Helped secure the election of his son Charles as King of the Romans
events.labelCn: 帮助其子查理当选罗马人的国王
events.note: John played a central role in the anti-Wittelsbach coalition that secured the election of his son Charles, the future Charles IV, in July 1346.

events.label: Was killed at the Battle of Crécy
events.note: Although completely blind by this stage of his life, John fought on the French side against Edward III of England and was killed at Crécy.

sourceNote: Basic card for the Bohemian succession.
notes:
Luxembourg king of Bohemia and father of Karl IV; killed at Crécy.

Research intake retained: John united the County of Luxembourg with the Bohemian crown through his marriage to the Přemyslid heiress Elisabeth. His reign established the territorial and dynastic platform from which his son Charles IV built the fourteenth-century Luxembourg imperial monarchy.

Confidence / caveats: His exact birthplace is not consistently stated in the stronger biographical material and is therefore left blank. His Polish kingship was a dynastic claim rather than effective rule and ended by treaty in 1335. John increasingly spent time outside Bohemia and often governed through lieutenants, but he remained the legal king until his death. His blindness was complete by the early 1340s.
